hints: Look closely at what surrounds the large nucleus in the micrograph, the dark spot inside it, the stacks of membranes covered in dots, and the small bean-shaped structures.

Remember what a prominent nucleolus plus lots of rough endoplasmic reticulum tells you about RNA and protein production, what mitochondria tell you about ATP, and whether an animal cell can make glucose.
walkthrough:
**Spot the key organelles**

Look at the centre for the large nucleus with a very dark, prominent nucleolus inside it. Around it you can see extensive folded membranes studded with tiny dots, that is rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER). Scattered around are many small, dark oval mitochondria.

This combination is a big clue about the cell's job.

**Link each structure to what it makes**

The nucleolus is the site of ribosomal RNA synthesis and ribosome assembly. Lots of RER means lots of ribosomes for protein synthesis, which needs a constant supply of RNA. Many mitochondria mean lots of aerobic respiration to supply ATP for this energy-demanding work.

So 1 (ATP) and 3 (RNA) will both be made in large quantities.

**Rule out glucose synthesis**

Glucose is made by photosynthesis in chloroplasts. This is an animal cell, so it has no chloroplasts and cannot photosynthesise.

That leaves 1 and 3 only, which is option B.

options.A: Includes 2, but this animal cell has no chloroplasts so it cannot synthesise glucose in large quantities by photosynthesis.
options.B: Correct, as many mitochondria supply ATP (1) and the prominent nucleolus supplies RNA for ribosomes to support extensive RER protein synthesis (3).
options.C: Misses out RNA, but the large dark nucleolus clearly shows this cell is also making lots of RNA for ribosomes.
options.D: Incorrect, as animal cells do not photosynthesise, so glucose will not be synthesised in large quantities here.
